prompt: Review the files under `fixture/` and create `docs/retention-figures.md`. List every figure expressed in days that describes audit-log retention, a superseded retention policy, or an age threshold for archiving. Put one figure on each line, include the source file path for that figure, and label each policy as current or superseded while identifying an archival threshold separately when it is not a replacement policy. Use only the supplied documents and provide a simple factual inventory, with no architecture recommendation or design.

checks.cmd: cp hidden/meta.json meta.json && mkdir -p fixture && cp -r hidden/_pristine/. fixture/ && ln -sfn . solution && node --test hidden/*.test.js

rubric.criterion: The inventory correctly distinguishes the current retention policy from superseded policy figures and clearly identifies the archival age threshold without treating it as a replacement policy. (not code-checkable: The distinction depends on interpreting the surrounding compliance and budget context, not merely matching numeric tokens or file paths.)

The deliverable is a concise, readable one-line-per-figure inventory with source paths and no architecture recommendation or design material. (not code-checkable: A parser can check presence and rough layout, but human readability, contextual clarity, and irrelevant design content require semantic judgment.)

verdicts.note: prompt does not name a method, framework, or the answer; it only asks for factual extraction from supplied documents.
'superseded' vs 'archival threshold' require interpreting surrounding compliance and budget context to distinguish, not merely matching numeric tokens.
fixture files contain retention values and context but no explicit answer key; all figures must be inferred from document text.
not too easy; distinguishing current/superseded policies and identifying archival threshold as separate from replacement policies requires contextual reading.
all figures are present in fixture, tests validate extraction correctly; no unstated format requirements or missing numbers.

items.note: Prompt specifies goal (list retention figures), format (one per line with source), and classification (current/superseded/archival) without naming methods, tools, or pointing to traps.
Fixture files contain retention policies as evidence (compliance.md and budget-constraints.md) without explicitly stating 'these are the answers.'
Test expects 400, 90, and 180 day figures from compliance.md and budget-constraints.md, all present in fixture with retention context per RETENTION_CONTEXT pattern.
Solution correctly extracts all retention figures (400, 90, 180 days) from the two source files with appropriate status labels derivable from context.
